text: The lambda architecture — last lesson's hybrid idea, given a specific name and shape.

A speed layer processes data fast and approximately, using an eventstream and KQL. A batch layer reprocesses everything slowly and exactly, using a databricks medallion pipeline. A serving layer merges both into one answer.

The real cost is maintaining two implementations of the same logic — KQL on one side, PySpark on the other, both computing the same aggregation. Any drift between them shows up as a fake discrepancy on the dashboard.
Teams still choose this when fast-and-approximate and slow-and-exact genuinely serve different purposes. Next up: the kappa architecture — the alternative that avoids maintaining two codepaths.
